newsitem.title: USA: L.A. municipal utility okays plan to expand sales.
newsitem.headline: L.A. municipal utility okays plan to expand sales.

text.p: The board of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) on Monday approved two ordinances aimed at boosting competitiveness, which were passed by voters in November.
One measure cleared the way for the utility to sell power under long-term contracts to entities outside the city limits, while the other addressed hiring of management employees.
Voters had also passed a third ballot intiative aimed at expanding investment options for the utility, but it was not on the board agenda.
As the electricity industry moves toward competition, LADWP has sought to improve efficiency, including cutting its workforce by 20 percent over the last two years.
The utility, which serves 1.3 million customers, last year announced plans to cut rates for large industrial customers, but the measure has languished at the city council.
The intiatives passed Tuesday must also be approved by the council.
In addition, LADWP is expected to select a "strategic alliance" with a major energy company in the near future. Final contenders for the role are Duke/Louis Dreyfus, Enron Corp and PacifiCorp.
